drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thanks—below is a revised draft that fills in the compensation and severance terms, adds standard executive protections (including defined Cause/Good Reason concepts and clearer termination mechanics), and narrows the restrictive covenant to a more reasonable scope. We’ve kept the structure aligned with your prior comments and are happy to incorporate any further market-based edits you’d like to propose.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of $350,000, payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices and subject to applicable withholdings. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in employee benefit plans generally available to senior executives of the Company, subject to the terms of those plans. The Executive shall also be eligible for an annual performance bonus of up to 40% of base salary, with the precise amount, if any, determined by the Board or its designee based on achievement of mutually agreed performance objectives.
edits.name: compensation

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause, or if the Executive resigns for Good Reason, then subject to the Executive’s execution and non-revocation of a customary general release of claims and continued compliance with this Agreement, the Company shall pay the Executive: (a) continued base salary for twelve (12) months; (b) a pro rata annual bonus for the year of termination, based on actual performance through the termination date; and (c) up to twelve (12) months of COBRA premium reimbursement, to the extent permitted by law and Company plan terms. All accrued but unpaid salary, earned bonus, and reimbursable expenses shall be paid in the ordinary course. No severance shall be payable upon termination for Cause or resignation without Good Reason.
edits.name: severance

edits.text: 4. NON-COMPETE. During employment and for six (6) months thereafter, the Executive shall not, within any jurisdiction in which the Company or its affiliates conduct material business as of the termination date, directly compete with the Company in a role that is materially similar to the Executive’s role and that would involve the development, marketing, or sale of products or services competitive with those of the Company. This restriction shall not prohibit passive ownership of less than 2% of a publicly traded company, nor shall it prevent the Executive from performing non-competitive services. The parties intend this covenant to be enforced to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, and if any provision is overbroad it shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to be enforceable.
edits.name: noncompete

edits.text: Include standard executive termination mechanics, including notice, opportunity to cure for Good Reason, and immediate cessation of duties upon termination as determined by the Company.
edits.name: termination mechanics

edits.text: Define Cause to include material misconduct, fraud, gross negligence, willful misconduct, material breach of duty, conviction or plea to certain crimes, and material violation of Company policies after notice and, where curable, a reasonable cure period.
edits.name: cause definition

edits.text: Define Good Reason to include a material reduction in authority, material reduction in base salary or target bonus, a required relocation beyond a reasonable commuting distance, or a material breach of the Agreement by the Company, in each case subject to prior written notice and an opportunity to cure.
edits.name: good reason definition
